For example, there's a Constitutional Amendment on the Missouri ballot this year which increases the tax on a pack of cigarettes, citing that Missouri has the lowest cigarette tax in the nation, with all money from the increased taxes going towards Pre-K education (while preventing politicians from touching the money).

On the face of it, it looks like a good deal, non-smokers don't pay anything and more money goes toward education.

But in reality the proposal is being pushed heavily by Big Tobacco because it also includes a bigger fee that would be placed on wholesalers of cigarettes who weren't part of the 1998 Master Settlement Agreement. So in reality it's all about trying to reduce competition by making it more expensive for smaller cigarette businesses to do business.

And on top of that, there's another legal way for politicians to essentially take the money. They can't touch the new money brought in by the amendment, but they can still touch the money from the general fund which was already allocated for that department.

So say the yearly budget for Pre-K education is $500,000 from the general fund and the new tax brings in $500,000 of new money. So that's $1,000,000 towards Pre-K education, right? Wrong, the politicians will simply cut $500,000 from the general fund that's put towards Pre-K education, resulting in a net gain of zero.

You should always be an informed voter, don't take political ads at their word, do your own research. Don't just read the small blurb about the ballot initiative on the ballot, look up the full wording and who's funding it and why they might want to be funding it. Increased funding for education is a HUGE red flag for this sort of thing, because people know that you can just tug on the heartstrings talking about money for education and most people will instantly vote for it.
Be especially wary of any ballot initiatives which are increasing taxes to pay for education. There's usually a more insidious motive behind them.
